$comment: ACKNOWLEDGED CHART DRIFT -- the reason this check can go GREEN.
Aaron 2026-09-05: 'we want to cleanup our drift and not just ignore it or
else everyting merged will be red forever in drift.'
He is right, and the first version of `--drift` had exactly that defect. It
failed whenever ANY chart was behind, and charts are ALWAYS somewhat behind --
argocd published 10.8.0 the day after we pinned 10.7.2. A check that is red on
every run is a check nobody reads, which is the cry-wolf failure `drift-loud.ts`
So drift is CARRIED, not ignored. Every entry names WHY the bump is not a bump
and what would close it. A chart NOT listed here going behind turns the check
red, which is the signal actually worth having.
AN ENTRY IS NOT A PARKING SPACE. `liftsWhen` must name a condition someone can
bring about, and the audit refuses an entry whose chart is no longer behind --
a stale acknowledgement is the same defect as an unacknowledged drift, pointed

acknowledged.reason: 162 releases behind, 8.7.0 -> 10.3.1, MAJOR. Measured 2026-09-04: 10.x requires THREE external dependencies we do not run (external object storage among them), and gitlab is already the single largest Application in the tree at 2525m -- over what one hosted runner can hold (2125m). The bump is a migration with a prerequisite list, not a version change.
acknowledged.liftsWhen: the three external dependencies exist and gitlab has governed resourceClaims so a dev rung can size it. Both are filed.

acknowledged.reason: 26 releases behind, 0.59.0 -> 1.6.0, MAJOR, and measured rather than assumed: `sql.driver` is renamed `sql.pluginName` (a bump that left the key alone would render, deploy, and point Temporal at no datastore), five bundled subcharts are removed upstream, and appVersion 1.27.2 -> 1.31.2 is a SERVER upgrade whose schema job runs versioned SQL migrations against CockroachDB that do not roll back cleanly. `numHistoryShards` is immutable after first deploy.
acknowledged.liftsWhen: the migration is done as its own change with its own testing -- and it is now on the critical path, because OpenSearch-backed visibility needs Temporal server >= 1.30.1.

acknowledged.reason: 7 releases behind, 88.6.3 -> 89.2.2, MAJOR. Not yet measured for breaking changes; a major on the chart that carries Prometheus, Alertmanager and Grafana touches the whole observability surface, and this tree's own `audit-observability-chain` pins the rendered shape of what it feeds.
acknowledged.liftsWhen: the 89.x changelog is read against our valuesObject and the observability roster is refreshed. This is a real bump nobody has costed yet, and saying so is the point of the entry.

acknowledged.reason: 16 releases behind, 0.24.2 -> 0.30.1. Every one is a 0.x MINOR, and semver gives 0.x minors no compatibility promise at all -- sixteen of them is a major in everything but the version string. spire is the identity substrate the decentralised-trust design depends on, so a silent behaviour change here is worse than being behind.
acknowledged.liftsWhen: the sixteen changelogs are read, or the bump is taken in stages with the live lane asserting spire Healthy at each one.

acknowledged.reason: 3 releases behind, 2.3.0 -> 3.1.0, MAJOR, published 2026-09-30 (3.0.0 landed after the last snapshot refresh, which is why this went red with nothing changed in the tree). NOT yet measured for breaking changes: a major on the chart that stores traces touches the OTLP ingest path, the storage/retention keys this tree sets (tempo.retention, the local trace path) and the datasource Grafana reads. Saying it is unmeasured is the point of the entry.
acknowledged.liftsWhen: the 3.x changelog is read against the tempo valuesObject and the observability roster (audit-observability-chain) is refreshed; filed as its own change.
